extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of Mark Twain / readers of collected letters and literary biography
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting passages from Mark Twain's late letters and recollections (1904–1905), including his remarks on literature, politics, and personal loss. The content is literary primary-source material rather than an instruction or formal guideline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization can degrade literature
rubrics_metrics.description: “It turned my stomach. It was not literature; yet it had been literature once—before I sold it to be degraded to an advertisement. I was going to write and ask you to melt the plates and put it out of print. But this morning I examined it without temper, and saw that if I abolished the advertisement it would be literature again.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clemens (Mark Twain) asserts that literary quality can be compromised when a work is tied to commercial uses (an 'advertisement'); removing the commercial element can restore the work's literary status. Context: he is discussing Adam's Diary and his revisions leading to Eve's Diary.
